newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian shares seen mixed, Tractebel strong.
newsitem.headline: Belgian shares seen mixed, Tractebel strong.

text.p: Belgian shares, underpinned throughout Wednesday by Tractebel fever, are likely to stick to narrow ranges ahead of Friday's reorganisation of the Bel-20 share index, traders said.
"Friday will be the big day. We don't expect much movement before then, although some people might try taking a bet on the outcome," one trader said.

The day's big news was the surge by utility holding company Tractebel It gained five percent at 14,800 francs -- a premium of 300 francs over the 14,500 franc bid announced late on Tuesday by Societe Generale de Belgique.

SGB ended two weeks of speculation on Tuesday with the announcement that it was raising its stake in Tractebel to 65 percent from 40 percent and making an offer at the same price of 14,500 francs per share for the remaining 35 percent.
However, in an effort to persuade private shareholders to hang onto their shares, it also announced a put warrant exercisable in November 1999 with a guaranteed price of 14,500 francs.
Share analysts variously estimated this warrant to be worth a premium of between 1,100 and 1,600 francs over the 14,500 franc share price, with a consequent boost to the market price.

SGB bought the 25 percent chunk of Tractebel on Tuesday from holding company Electrafina and insurer Royale Belge for a total price of 49 billion francs of which 41 billion goes to Electrafina and eight billion to Royale Belge.
In both cases, roughly half the amount was capital gain.
Electrafina ended Wednesday 50 francs up at 2,900, and Royale Belge finished 90 francs higher at 6,020.
SGB and Groupe Bruxelles Lambert (GBL), the company that controls both Electrafina and Royale Belge, barely reacted to the news of The tractebel deal.
SGB rose 15 francs to 2,555. GBL added 5 francs to 3,850.
More than 85,000 Tractebel shares changed hands during the day, so that the share accounted for more than one-third of the healthy 3.1 billion francs turnover in Belgian shares.
Other shares of note were Powerfin which ended 1.5 percent lower at 4,705 francs. Traders said it was losing ground as shareholders reshuffled their portfolios.
Fast food retailer Quick, which on Tuesday lost more than 10 percent, bounced back more than five percent to 2,410 francs on Wednesday in what traders said could only have been a technical rebound.
Non-ferrous metals firm Union Miniere, which on Tuesday posted a 30 percent drop in group net profit in the first half of the year, ended 15 francs down at 2,365.
Traders said the negative effects of the corporate result were being offset by the positive influence of the re-weighting of the share in the index on Friday.
The Bel-20 index .BFR ended the day 1.50 points or 0.09 percent down at 1,754.65 in a 1,765.97/1,751.91. There were nine gainers, one share was unchanged and 10 were down.
